title: Residual base-change equality for explicitly constructed open comparisons
statement: Let f:X→S, f′:X′→S′, g:S′→S and g′:X′→X form a cartesian square [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-base-change], and let K∈D(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category]. Let V⊆S and V′⊆S′ be opens with V′⊆g⁻¹V, put U=f⁻¹V and U′=f′⁻¹V′, and let j:U′→U satisfy j≫U.ι=U′.ι≫g′, with the restricted square cartesian. Write K₀=K|U, R=restriction to V′, and R′=restriction to U′ [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps]. Define δ:L(j)*K₀→R′(L(g′)*K) by singleComplexRestrictedCoefficient of the identity [def-pc-single-complex-open-restriction-data]. For the explicit maps a=singleComplexOpenBaseChangeSourceIso f g K V V′ hV′ and b=singleComplexOpenDirectImageIso f′ V′ [def-pc-n3-open-base-change-comparisons], R(baseChange(K)) = a.hom ≫ baseChange₀(K₀) ≫ R(f′|V′)_*(δ) ≫ b.inv.app(L(g′)*K) [def-pc-derived-base-change-map]. This asserts only equality for fixed, already constructed data, with no existential comparison claim.

proof.text: On K-injective models the explicit direct-image comparison is the sectionwise identity. Restriction preserves K-injectives and is exact. The canonical derived-functor factorization equations therefore identify its counit with the restriction of the pinned original counit. In notation L₀=L(f|V)*, R_X=restriction to U and R_S=restriction to V, with c_f:L₀R_S≅R_XLf* built from the open pullback/composition comparisons and b_f the explicit direct-image comparison, the equation is L₀(b_f.hom.app E)≫ε_f₀.app(R_X E)=c_f.hom.app(Rf*E)≫R_X(ε_f.app E). On representatives both sides evaluate the same restricted tensor-pullback counit. Use this for f and f′.

Transpose the displayed equation under the pinned adjunction for f′ restricted to V′. Substitute the counit compatibility from step 1 and the explicit source comparison. The associativity laws for pullback composition, hj and the commutative square identify the pullback paths; cancel inverse comparison factors. The factors left on the coefficient side are exactly singleComplexRestrictedCoefficient of the identity. Injectivity of the Hom equivalence gives the equation. This argument is valid for empty opens and zero coefficients.

theorem singleComplexOpen_baseChange_calculation
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{u},
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g : S' ⟶ S) (g' : X' ⟶ X)
    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (K : schemeDerivedCategory X)
    (V : S.Opens) (V' : S'.Opens) (hV' : V' ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ V)
    (j : (f' ⁻¹ᵁ V').toScheme ⟶ (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme)
    (hj : j ≫ (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι = (f' ⁻¹ᵁ V').ι ≫ g')
    (sq₀ : IsPullback j (f' ∣_ V') (f ∣_ V) (g.resLE V V' hV')) :
    let K₀ := (schemeOpenRestriction X (f ⁻¹ᵁ V)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K
    let R := (schemeOpenRestriction S' V').mapDerivedCategory
    let δ := singleComplexRestrictedCoefficient g' K ((derivedPullback g').obj K) (𝟙 _)
      (f ⁻¹ᵁ V) (f' ⁻¹ᵁ V') j hj
    R.map (schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap f f' g g' sq.w K) =
      (singleComplexOpenBaseChangeSourceIso f g K V V' hV').hom ≫
        schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap
          (f ∣_ V) (f' ∣_ V') (g.resLE V V' hV') j sq₀.w K₀ ≫
        (schemeDerivedDirectImage (f' ∣_ V')).map δ ≫
        (singleComplexOpenDirectImageIso f' V').inv.app ((derivedPullback g').obj K)
